title: Are the real multilinear Bohnenblust–Hille constants bounded?
credit: Bohnenblust–Hille (1931); boundedness/universality question Pellegrino–Teixeira (2016), Diniz et al. (2014).
premise_risks: Appears on Tao's optimization-constants list (26b), so the problem is known; it is not actively moving there
Real and complex constants differ; this candidate is for real scalars
plain: Take an m-linear form T on n-dimensional real space with the max norm, and look at its coefficients T(e_{j1},...,e_{jm}). The Bohnenblust–Hille inequality says that the l^{2m/(m+1)}-norm of these coefficients is at most B_m times the supremum of |T| over the unit cube, with B_m not depending on n. For m=2 the best constant is sqrt 2 (Littlewood's 4/3 inequality). Do the best constants B_m stay bounded as m grows, as conjectured (B_m = 2^{1-1/m}, tending to 2), or do they go to infinity?
math: For real $m$-linear $T:(\mathbb R^n)^m\to\mathbb R$ let $\|T\|=\sup\{|T(x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(m)})|:\|x^{(i)}\|_\infty\le1\}$ and let $B_{\mathbb R,m}=\sup_{n\ge1}\sup_{T\ne0}\big(\sum_{j\in[n]^m}|T(e_{j_1},\dots,e_{j_m})|^{\frac{2m}{m+1}}\big)^{\frac{m+1}{2m}}/\|T\|$. Prove or disprove: $\sup_{m\ge1}B_{\mathbb R,m}<\infty$. (Known: $2^{1-1/m}\le B_{\mathbb R,m}<1.3\,m^{0.365}$ for $m\ge14$; conjecturally $B_{\mathbb R,m}=2^{1-1/m}$.)
